lesson.child_mission: Choreography organises movement into a structure such as ABA (idea, contrast, return) or narrative beginning–middle–end. A motif is a short movement idea you can repeat, vary or reverse. Repetition helps the audience remember the motif.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Invent a three-move motif and describe an ABA plan using it.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Motif: step-clap-spiral. A: full size; B: floor version; A: full size ending in freeze.'

WATCH FOR
Making unrelated moves with no repeat. Motifs unify a dance.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Choreograph a 24-count ABA dance with a written motif and labels for A and B. Perform and ask a viewer what motif they noticed.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.explain:
Choreography organises movement into a structure such as ABA (idea, contrast, return) or narrative beginning–middle–end. A motif is a short movement idea you can repeat, vary or reverse. Repetition helps the audience remember the motif.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

HOW TO WORK
Read the worked example and name the elements, techniques or performance choices that carry the idea. Before looking at the correction, make your own attempt using the exact question provided. For movement or instruments, use a clear space, ask an adult to be nearby and stop if anything feels unsafe. You may always describe a choice instead of performing it. One deliberate artistic choice with a named effect is more useful than a longer praise sentence.
teach_steps.notice: Making unrelated moves with no repeat. Motifs unify a dance. Name the element or technique and its effect, not just decoration.
